Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to: a. improve the quality of life of women, children and the quality of families; b. increase the institutional capacity of women's empowerment and child protection in the regions, including the development of gender and child data systems; and

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1

EXPLANATION
O F
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASURUAN REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2018
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
The State as the mandate holder of people's sovereignty is responsible for implementing development to achieve public welfare. This is as mandated by the constitution which has become a national consensus for the Indonesian nation. The 1945 Constitution is the fundamental legal foundation (Fundamental Norm) in formulating the direction and basis for social, political, and state legal policy-making.

The State as an organization certainly always has objectives as stated in the fourth paragraph of the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states: "Furthermore, to form a Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia that protects the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation, and participate in implementing world order based on freedom, eternal peace and social justice." Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the purpose of establishing regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Explicitly, the objectives of the Indonesian State reflect several national objectives of the Indonesian nation. The objectives contained in this fourth paragraph constitute the constitutional promise of the Indonesian state to all its people while simultaneously becoming the basic rights of society. Therefore, the State is obligated to make various efforts in order to fulfill the constitutional rights of its citizens.

One of these four objectives is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory as well as promote general welfare. This means that the Indonesian nation must be free from all forms of actions that can harm its citizens, efforts to maintain this conduciveness are carried out in order to create a prosperous and beneficial social life without looking at certain groups and classes, because the meaning of the entire nation is a reflection for all Indonesian society without exception, whether men, women or children.

The protection that is the State's responsibility is not only for every person both in the individual and group sense along with the cultural identity attached to them, but this protection must also be interpreted as an endeavor to promote general welfare for the entire nation. So there need to be steps that must be taken by the State to achieve the above objectives by empowering its people, especially those who have been viewed as weak and marginalized. Based on these considerations, the Pasuruan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a concrete step in order to protect the entire nation and promote general welfare.

From the above description, it is clearly explained that based on article 18 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, regional governments have the authority to make regulations related to regional needs in order to accommodate regional potential and local wisdom according to their respective localistic needs. Whereas for Pasuruan Regency has a distinctive character as a santri city that is thick with the values of its religious teachings. From the perspective of Islam, women's empowerment and child protection are highly upheld, even when Islam was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad SAW. The condition of the Arab nation at that time greatly looked down on the status of women. This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time it seemed as if there was no protection at all for the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services for women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

AMENDMENT TO BUPATI PASURUAN REGULATION NUMBER 69 OF 2014 CONCERNING GUIDELINES FOR GRANTING FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO POLITICAL PARTIES

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

BUPATI PASURUAN,

Considering : a. that to implement the provisions of Article 39 paragraph (1) letter d of Law Number 2 of 2011 concerning Amendments to Law Number 2 of 2008 concerning Political Parties, the Pasuruan Regency Government has issued Bupati Pasuruan Regulation Number 69 of 2014 concerning Guidelines for Granting Financial Assistance to Political Parties;

EXPLANATION
O F
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASURUAN REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2018
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
The State as the mandate holder of people's sovereignty is responsible for implementing development to achieve public welfare. This is as mandated by the constitution which has become a national consensus for the Indonesian nation. The 1945 Constitution is the fundamental legal foundation (Fundamental Norm) in formulating the direction and basis for social, political, and state legal policy-making.

The State as an organization certainly always has objectives as stated in the fourth paragraph of the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states: "Furthermore, to form a Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia that protects the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation, and participate in implementing world order based on freedom, eternal peace and social justice." Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the purpose of establishing regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Explicitly, the objectives of the Indonesian State reflect several national objectives of the Indonesian nation. The objectives contained in this fourth paragraph constitute the constitutional promise of the Indonesian state to all its people while simultaneously becoming the basic rights of society. Therefore, the State is obligated to make various efforts in order to fulfill the constitutional rights of its citizens.

One of these four objectives is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory as well as promote general welfare. This means that the Indonesian nation must be free from all forms of actions that can harm its citizens, efforts to maintain this conduciveness are carried out in order to create a prosperous and beneficial social life without looking at certain groups and classes, because the meaning of the entire nation is a reflection for all Indonesian society without exception, whether men, women or children.

The protection that is the State's responsibility is not only for every person both in the individual and group sense along with the cultural identity attached to them, but this protection must also be interpreted as an endeavor to promote general welfare for the entire nation. So there need to be steps that must be taken by the State to achieve the above objectives by empowering its people, especially those who have been viewed as weak and marginalized. Based on these considerations, the Pasuruan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a concrete step in order to protect the entire nation and promote general welfare.

From the above description, it is clearly explained that based on article 18 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, regional governments have the authority to make regulations related to regional needs in order to accommodate regional potential and local wisdom according to their respective localistic needs. Whereas for Pasuruan Regency has a distinctive character as a santri city that is thick with the values of its religious teachings. From the perspective of Islam, women's empowerment and child protection are highly upheld, even when Islam was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad SAW. The condition of the Arab nation at that time greatly looked down on the status of women. This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time it seemed as if there was no protection at all for the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services for women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pasuruan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Pasuruan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pasuruan.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Government of Pasuruan Regency.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person (human being) who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children and breastfeed.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
11. Women's Empowerment is a systematic and planned effort to achieve gender equality and justice in family and community life.
12. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity and budgeting that takes into account differences in needs, experiences and aspirations of men and women.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in providing assistance and has professional competence in their field.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions during the service process.
18. Institution is an Office/Agency/Bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
19. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as PPTPPA, is an institution/functional work unit providing integrated services and assistance, counseling, referral and advocacy for women and children victims of violence.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
21. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 4
In order to realize the objectives as referred to in Article 3 letter a, this shall be carried out through:
a. providing access for women and children to education services, health and other strategic fields;
b. encouraging the involvement of women and children in the development process; c. providing knowledge, skills, character values, morals and family resilience; and
d. encouraging programs that can increase the independence of women in the economic, political, legal, social, cultural and other strategic fields.

Article 6
In order to implement the objectives as referred to in Article 3 letter c, it shall be carried out through promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time it seemed as if there was no protection at all for the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services for women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

5.3.rationale: The regulation mentions “kearifan lokal” and local distinctiveness in the explanatory background, and it allows broad community participation (Pasal 26–27) and includes “tokoh masyarakat” as possible management elements (Pasal 17(2), 19(2), 21(2)). However, it does not specifically call out traditional/cultural institutions/leaders (adat bodies, cultural councils) or set a mechanism for engaging them. General community participation is not the same as explicit traditional/cultural engagement. Hence the golden ‘Yes’ is not clearly grounded in the Indonesian text; the judge’s ‘No’ is reasonable.
